candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Handling Hazardous and Infectious Materials / hazardous-drug spill response
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to a hazardous antineoplastic drug spill by following the facility hazardous-drug spill SOP, using the designated spill kit and appropriate PPE, and obtaining trained assistance when required.

options.A: Initiate the facility hazardous-drug spill procedure, obtain the designated spill kit and required PPE, and obtain trained assistance if required
options.B: Wipe up the drug immediately with routine unit cleaning supplies while wearing only standard examination gloves
options.C: Use a standard infectious-waste cleanup kit because hazardous-drug spills are managed the same way as biohazard spills
options.D: Leave the spill unattended until environmental services arrives, without initiating the hazardous-drug spill procedure

candidate.rationale: OSHA guidance states that healthcare settings where hazardous drugs are administered should have hazardous-drug spill kits available and that facilities should maintain spill-management SOPs. Workers involved in spill management should be trained; appropriate PPE is donned before cleanup, the spill kit is used to contain the spill, and trained help is obtained when needed. The spill size may determine who is authorized to perform cleanup. Routine supplies or an infectious-waste kit are not substitutes for the hazardous-drug procedure, and the area should not be left without initiating the facility response. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hazardous-drug spills should be managed under a facility spill SOP with a designated hazardous-drug spill kit, appropriate PPE, and trained personnel/assistance as required by the spill circumstances.
candidate.source_document_title: Hazardous Drugs — Controlling Occupational Exposure to Hazardous Drugs
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Spill Kits' and 'Clean-up of Spills': spill kits containing materials needed to clean hazardous-drug spills should be available; each facility should have SOPs for spill management; workers involved should be trained; spill size may determine who is authorized; general spill procedure includes assessing the spill, obtaining the spill kit, donning PPE, obtaining trained help if necessary, and containing the spill with the kit
